content: 1. Cefoxitin can decrease the effectiveness of the BCG live vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. It is contraindicated to administer the live bacterial vaccine until the completion of antibiotic therapy. 2. Chloramphenicol reduces the effects of cefoxitin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid using these drugs together or consider an alternative therapy, as bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the activity of bactericidal agents. 3. Cefoxitin reduces the efficacy of the cholera vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration of systemic antibiotics with the cholera vaccine, as these antibiotics may act against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 4. Cefoxitin may decrease the effects of atezolizumab, a checkpoint inhibitor, through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 5. Cefoxitin may reduce the effects of avelumab, another immune checkpoint inhibitor, through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as coadministration may compromise the therapeutic efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 6. Azithromycin decreases the effects of cefoxitin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely, as bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the activity of bactericidal agents. 7. Cefoxitin reduces the effects of aztreonam by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Increased production of beta-lactamases induced by cefoxitin can inactivate aztreonam. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Cefoxitin may decrease the effects of balstilimab, an immune checkpoint inhibitor, through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 9. Cefoxitin can reduce the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of cefoxitin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely, as bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the activity of bactericidal agents. 11. Cefoxitin can reduce the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but an alternative or additional form of birth control may be advisable during concomitant use. 15. Cefoxitin may reduce the effects of dostarlimab, an immune checkpoint inhibitor, through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as coadministration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 16. Cefoxitin increases the toxicity of gentamicin through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely, as cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. 23. Cefoxitin increases the toxicity of kanamycin through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely, as cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. 24. Minocycline decreases the effects of cefoxitin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely, as cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. 30. Coadministration with antibiotics reduces efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Use caution and monitor closely, as cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. 35. Tetracycline decreases the effects of cefoxitin via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Coadministration of cefoxitin and voclosporin may increase the toxicity of either drug through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely, as the risk of acute and/or chronic nephrotoxicity may be elevated. 40. Cefoxitin increases the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Cefoxitin increases the levels or effects of choline magnesium trisalicylate by competing for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 42. Cefoxitin increases the toxicity of furosemide through pharmacodynamic synergism. This interaction is minor, but there is an increased risk of nephrotoxicity. Monitor closely. 43. Rose hips increase the levels or effects of cefoxitin by competing for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Monitor closely.
